title: Maskachoung / Maskutchoung
summary: Maskachoung, also written Maskutchoung, is recorded as a Native placename associated with a neck of land on the southern part of the Hempstead Plains. Strong discusses George Weeks's listing of Maskutchoung as a Native community near Hempstead. The name is interpreted as a grassland or prairie place.
address_label: Southern Hempstead Plains / East Meadow area
ancestral_territory_note: Linked to Merrick Ancestral Land as an interior Hempstead Plains placename and Native community reference near the south shore homeland.
why_this_matters: Maskachoung shows that Merrick ancestral land was not only shoreline and bay. The Hempstead Plains were also Native geography, remembered through names for grassland, prairie, community, and movement between the interior and the south shore.
introduction_content: Maskachoung / Maskutchoung belongs to the Hempstead Plains and East Meadow area, where grassland, planting, hunting, and travel landscapes connected the interior plain to Merrick south shore homelands.
history_content: The history preserves a Hempstead Plains placename connected with grassland geography. Later historical discussion treats Maskutchoung as a village community near Hempstead and separates it from unrelated Cutchogue explanations.
translation_content:
The name is interpreted as on the grass land or in the prairie. Recorded forms include Maskachoung and Maskutchoung. The interpretation draws on related Algonquian words for grassland or prairie plus a locative ending.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place-names are part of our everyday lives, and at one level they simply label places. But the names of places are a fascinating part of our heritage, most of them fully meaningful when first coined.”

— Scottish Name Studies Board, Place-name stories (n.d.), Why study place-names? introduction
whereintheworld_content: This blue marker is an approximate general-location point for the Hempstead Plains area near the modern preserve at Nassau Community College. It is not an exact historic neck, village, or boundary coordinate.
